label: conj:hecke-monodromy-step-two
title: The Hecke quadratic is the q-deformed branch-point monodromy of the colour cubic (Step 2 of the canonical chain as a conjecture)
html:
Conjecture (Step 2 as monodromy). Let P(X, z) = X^3 + (z+1)X^2 + (z^2+z+1)X + (z^3+z^2+z+1) be the colour cubic, whose root X(z) and its jets are the Seiberg--Witten periods, and let \Delta \subset \mathbb{C} be its discriminant locus in z. The substrate connection on \mathbb{C} \setminus \Delta has braid-group monodromy \varrho \colon B_n \to H_n(q) into the Hecke tower carrying the Markov trace, such that for every generator g_i = \varrho(\sigma_i):

  1. the Hecke quadratic g_i^2 = (q - q^{-1})\, g_i + 1 holds, together with the braid relation g_i g_{i+1} g_i = g_{i+1} g_i g_{i+1} and far commutation;
  2. under the classical specialisation \varepsilon \colon H_n(q) \to \mathbb{Q}S_n each g_i becomes an involution, \varepsilon(g_i)^2 = 1 --- the Picard--Lefschetz transposition of the two roots of P that collide at a branch point.

The two Stokes eigenvalues q and -q^{-1} of the curvature polynomial F(\sigma) = \sigma^2 - (q - q^{-1})\sigma - 1 are then a consequence: (g_i - q)(g_i + q^{-1}) = 0.

What is derived and what is conjectured

The discriminant is the reciprocal irreducible sextic 16z^6 + 24z^5 + 35z^4 + 50z^3 + 35z^2 + 24z + 16, with six simple complex branch points and no branching at infinity. Continuing the three roots of P around each branch point gives a transposition every time; three distinct transpositions occur, so the monodromy group is S_3, and the ordered product of the six local monodromies is the identity. On the two colliding roots a transposition is the swap, an involution with eigenvalues \pm 1 and minimal polynomial \sigma^2 - 1 = (\sigma - q)(\sigma + q^{-1})|_{q=1}. So item 2, and the q = 1 specialisation of item 1, are theorems about the geometry the framework already carries. Pushing item 1 through \varepsilon and using item 2 forces \varepsilon\bigl((q - q^{-1})\, g_i\bigr) = 0: the classical shadow forgets exactly the deformation parameter.

What remains conjectural is the deformation 1 \mapsto q itself: no connection with q-deformed monodromy has been constructed, and the curvature form the chain names is stipulated rather than computed. The literature model is Kohno--Drinfeld: the monodromy of a Knizhnik--Zamolodchikov connection factors through H_n(q). At real level that monodromy has unit-modulus eigenvalues, which the real substrate pin q_0 \approx 1.11 is not; a Knizhnik--Zamolodchikov realisation therefore requires the non-unitary level k + 2 = 2\pi i/\ln q_0 \approx 60.218\, i in the convention q = e^{2\pi i/(k+2)}. Whether the substrate connection is such a connection is the open construction. That hypothesis now has a name, QOU.Mass.KZPullbackGenerators: each substrate generator is conjugate in the tower to a monodromy generator of the \mathfrak{sl}_2 Knizhnik--Zamolodchikov connection on \mathrm{Conf}_3(\mathbb{C}) pulled back along the root map z \mapsto \{X_1(z), X_2(z), X_3(z)\} at the level fixed by the substrate parameter (k + 2 = i\pi/\ln q_0 in Kohno's convention q = e^{i\pi/(k+2)}, q_0 an input), and from that class the Hecke quadratic is derived rather than assumed. What is established on the way, and what is not: the six branch points are fixed, so the base is \mathbb{C} \setminus \Delta with free fundamental group and the braid group enters only through the root map; every lasso lifts to a positive half-twist, the six composing to the full twist \Delta^2 (probe, 13/13); the convention-D Markov parameter z_D = q^3/(q^2+1) is exactly the U_q(\mathfrak{sl}_2) fundamental quantum trace, and \mathfrak{sl}_3 never reproduces it (QOU.Mass.SL2QuantumTraceIsZD); flatness of a Knizhnik--Zamolodchikov connection is independent of the level (QOU.Mass.KZFlatnessLevelIndependent), so the level enters only through the monodromy's target. Constructing the connection itself, and hence an instance of the class, remains open.

A second route to the same deformation --- the family's own periods, rather than an imported Knizhnik--Zamolodchikov connection --- is now narrowed from both sides, and the narrowing is negative. The framework's one candidate connection on this family is the abelianised Cartan form A^0 = X\,dz, which is the Seiberg--Witten differential itself; its push-down \sum_j X_j\,dz = -(z+1)\,dz is exact by Vieta, and around every branch point both the fixed sheet's circle integral and the exchanged pair's sum vanish to 10^{-30} at 50 digits, so every lasso has holonomy 1 (probe colour_cubic_abelian_twist_holonomy_probe, 8/8). That connection supplies no twist. Untwisted periods fare no better in principle: Gauss--Manin monodromy on such a family is quasi-unipotent, and an eigenvalue of finite order --- or, more generally, a quasi-unipotent one --- is never a real number greater than one (QOU.Mass.UntwistedMonodromyPrune), so neither q_0 \approx 1.11 nor -q_0^{-1} can arise that way. What survives is a twisted period: a local system with exponent \mu, whose pseudo-reflection monodromy has eigenvalues \{1, e^{2\pi i \mu}\}. Matching the Hecke ratio forces e^{2\pi i \mu} = -q^2, and that forces \operatorname{Im} \mu = -\ln q / \pi, which is non-zero for every q > 1 (QOU.Mass.TwistedPeriodEigenvalueRatio); so no unitary local system, no rational twist and no root-of-unity twist can carry the deformation. The exponent is where q_0 enters, and it enters as an input: \mu(q_0) is a label for the substrate parameter, not a derivation of it. Whether such a twisted family exists on \mathbb{C} \setminus \Delta is the open construction on this route, exactly as an instance of QOU.Mass.KZPullbackGenerators is on the other.

Lean structure

The class QOU.Mass.HeckeMonodromy carries items 1 and 2 as its four fields (quad, braid, far_comm, shadow_involution). Derived from it without further hypotheses: hecke_factor (the eigenvalue factorisation), shadow_hecke_at_one, shadow_kills_h, and shadow_coxeter (the shadow generators satisfy the Coxeter presentation of S_n: involution, braid relation, far commutation, so \varepsilon \circ \varrho is a permutation representation, as the computed S_3 requires). The classical shadow itself is proved unconditionally in QOU.Mass.HeckeQuadraticClassicalShadow (the swap is an involution satisfying the q = 1 quadratic), and the unit-modulus obstruction in QOU.Mass.KZUnitModulusPrune. Two facts the probe measured about the discriminant are theorems in QOU.Mass.ColourCubicDiscriminant and its archimedean companion: the sextic is reciprocal, z^6 D(z^{-1}) = D(z), and it is the sum of squares (4z^3 + 3z^2 + 3z + 4)^2 + 2z^2(z^2 + 1), so it has no real root and every branch point is non-real (no_real_branch_point).
